independentReview.reason: TWO APPROVES at this exact head, after four consecutive rounds of REQUEST CHANGES at earlier heads. The refusals are recorded rather than smoothed over because they are what makes this approval worth anything, and every one of them is the same disease in different clothes: a check that reads as verification while verifying less. ROUND 1: a citation was validated by the cited commit's SUBJECT alone. ROUND 2: two reviewers independently refused because this repository ends nearly every subject with its governing issue number, so 'PR [#300](...) (952ce309)' and 'PR [#240](...) (d59c3d65)' both certified TRUE - #300 is an OPEN ISSUE and 952ce309 is a lane commit that never landed. The writer confirmed both against git rather than taking the reports on trust. Fixed by requiring the SHA to sit on origin/main's first-parent chain AND the subject to name that PR, two conditions that fail independently. The same round found mergeCitations read two join shapes and silently skipped a third the document was already using twice, so a live assertion covering 9 of 11 citations read as full verification - issue #330's failure, a rule passing because its anchor is absent. ROUND 3: an adversarial reviewer showed the 200-character citation window made a pairing INVISIBLE rather than flagged when enough prose sat between the PR link and its SHA, and that widening it to 2000 produced five spurious pairings, proving 200 was an accidental fit. The window was deleted outright; coverage moved to a separate critic, uncitedLandings, which reds any real landing no citation covers and THROWS if its landing reader is omitted so it cannot degrade into 'all cited'. ROUND 4: the adversarial reviewer refused on the guard's own comments - uncitedLandings's docstring named two ways a false claim stays invisible and asserted 'Both cases are pinned in the suite' when only one had a test, so the file whose purpose is to stop a document asserting untrue things about its own verification was doing exactly that one level down. Fixed by making the claim TRUE rather than weakening it: the second limit got its own test, and the docstring now gives each case its own reason instead of one reason that only fit the second. The writer also corrected its own earlier understatement of the limit's width - an invented PR number and an invented SHA in free prose are equally invisible and need no prior citation to hide behind. ROUND 5, this head: the correctness reviewer completed the full local gate in its own clone and independently re-derived every SHA, ancestry and subject claim in the lane's messages, including that 952ce309 is not an ancestor of origin/main despite carrying #300 in its subject; it raised ONE NON-BLOCKING finding, that the refSplit docblock sits ~137 lines from refSplit after round 2's insertion, which is recorded and queued as its own lane rather than stacked unreviewed onto an approved head. The adversarial reviewer ran EIGHT mutations against the guard and confirmed each reds BY TEST NAME rather than by count - the landing requirement, reallyLanded, the subject match, the squash branch, an emptied exception list, a dead exception entry, the citation regex widened to bind free prose, and one join shape removed - proved by mutation rather than inference that the test added at this head is not vacuous, replanted the original historical defect and confirmed the live-record test catches it, and independently reproduced the 200-versus-2000 measurement by extracting the LITERAL old regex from b4b49bf9:317 rather than reimplementing it from prose. On that last point the writer had, at the previous head, carried a number from a report instead of measuring it, a round-4 reviewer was right to call it unreproducible, and it was re-measured by the writer and then by a reviewer before it was allowed to stand.
